html:
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was the Ottoman officer who founded the Republic of Turkey and led it as its first president from 1923 until his death in 1938.

Born in Salonica, he made his name defending Gallipoli against the Allies in 1915. After the Ottoman defeat in the First World War, the Allies and Greece moved to carve up Anatolia. Kemal organised resistance from Ankara and won the War of Independence. The Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 recognised the new Turkey.

He then remade the country from the top down:

  • He ended the sultanate in 1922 and abolished the caliphate in 1924.
  • The Civil Code of 1926 replaced religious family law.
  • The Latin alphabet replaced Arabic script in 1928.
  • Women won the vote in 1934, and everyone took surnames; the parliament gave him "Atatürk", father of the Turks.

He ruled through one party and put down Kurdish revolts by force. His secular nationalism, called Kemalism, shaped Turkey for the rest of the century.
sum: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was the Ottoman officer who founded the Republic of Turkey and led it as its first president from 1923 until his death in 1938.
